correctness.rationale: Bargetz--Bartoš--Kubiś--Luggin identify 1-homogeneity with vertex-transitivity of the distance-colored complete graph, prove \(\delta(X)\le(n+|S_X|)/2\), give the exact odd case, and construct the even lower bound. Edmonds' Theorem 1.4 bounds the number of odd color valencies by the maximal number of involutions in a group of order \(n\); Theorem 1.2 gives that maximum as \(n/2+n_2/2-1\) for even \(n\). Every positive singleton distance has valency one, so including zero gives \(|S_X|\le n/2+n_2/2\), yielding the claimed upper bound. The source construction with \(n=2^a(2k+1)\) has \(2^{a-1}(3k+2)=(3n+n_2)/4\), so equality follows.
correctness.risk: The proof imports Edmonds' published finite-group extremum rather than reproving it.

value.rationale: The theorem closes an explicit exact-value problem for a natural invariant of finite homogeneous metric spaces in every cardinality. It turns a lower-bound family into a complete formula and reveals the precise dependence on the 2-adic part of \(n\).
value.risk: It determines the extremal count but does not classify all extremal metric spaces.

final_claim: Let \(\Delta_1(n)\) be the maximum number of attained distances, including zero, in an \(n\)-point finite \(1\)-homogeneous metric space. If \(n\) is odd then \(\Delta_1(n)=(n+1)/2\). If \(n\) is even and \(n_2\) is the largest power of two dividing \(n\), then \(\Delta_1(n)=(3n+n_2)/4\).
limitations: No classification of all spaces attaining the maximum is claimed.
